claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship the upgrade path with the component itself; a migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Component state migrations are a new Pulumi feature.
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
A GitHub discussion for component state migrations feedback exists at github.com/pulumi/pulumi/discussions/24799.
A Pulumi docs page exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/state-migrations/ covering component state migrations and the callback contract.
The pulumi/examples repository contains an example at aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration with three programs (v1, v2, v3) and migration code, and a README for v1.
A Components docs page exists at /docs/iac/concepts/components/.
The legacy AWSX VPC component is `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc`; in the example's first version it creates a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and its association, and an internet gateway.
Replacing an AWS VPC would require replacing a security group that refers to the VPC's ID (per AWS CloudFormation EC2 SecurityGroup VpcId documentation).
Without a migration connecting old state to new code, upgrading from the legacy AWSX VPC component to the modern one could replace the VPC instead of keeping it.
The example does not create a database.
When a database is recreated as a replacement, the replacement does not automatically contain the old data.
The modern AWSX VPC component is `awsx.ec2.Vpc`, and the second version of the example upgrades to it while keeping the existing network.
The third version of the example removes AWSX and declares the resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.

The resource trees Pulumi tracks: v1 has awsx:x:ec2:Vpc with children including awsx:x:ec2:Subnet and awsx:x:ec2:InternetGateway wrappers; v2 has awsx:ec2:Vpc with aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc under it and subnet 'vpc-isolated-1' and internet gateway under the VPC; v3 has plain aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc as root.
Each record in Pulumi's state has a Pulumi name called a URN, and managed resources also have an ID from the cloud provider.
The legacy AWSX component wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components; modern AWSX removes those wrappers and puts managed resources under different parents.
In the example, the Pulumi name of the subnet changes from `vpc-isolated-0` to `vpc-isolated-1` between legacy and modern AWSX.
Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when its saved state remains compatible, but cannot remove component wrappers and transfer references to replacement resources.
Pulumi component resources accept a `stateMigrations` option that takes a migration callback, and the new VPC component is registered with an alias for the legacy component type.
With an alias, Pulumi finds the old component; the migration callback receives the old component's saved state followed by the state of its children.

A state migration callback returns `newState` (the complete set of records replacing the old component and its children) and `successors` (a map from each old URN that disappears to the URN that takes its place).
The example's migration callback is safe to run again: if state already uses modern AWSX or plain AWS resources it does nothing, and an unexpected component type raises an error.
The example's `rename` helper copies the saved record and changes its URN, type, and parent, preserving the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.

Entries in `successors` let the Pulumi engine know that the old component wrapper and managed subnet point to the same new subnet record, and Pulumi uses these mappings to update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, such as the security group's reference to the VPC.
The second migration removes the AWSX VPC component record and moves the managed VPC into its place; both the old component and its VPC child map to the new VPC record, and the VPC keeps its AWS ID.
The plain VPC registration keeps aliases for both previous component types and both migration callbacks.
Pulumi runs state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next callback.
A stack still using legacy AWSX can upgrade directly to the plain AWS version, and a stack already using modern AWSX skips the first migration.
Once both migrations have run, both callbacks return no result on later updates.
After a state migration, Pulumi compares the new program with the migrated state and calls the provider for remaining changes.
In the example, upgrades can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
Running `pulumi preview` before each upgrade should show no creates, deletes, or replacements for the existing VPC, subnet, route table, association, internet gateway, and security group.
Pulumi preview evaluates the state migration without saving it, and the update (`pulumi up`) saves the migrated state.

When a component registers the migration in its implementation, users do not need to write the migration, attach the callback, or edit stack state; Pulumi runs the migration as part of normal preview and update.
For an internal component change that keeps the same inputs and outputs, users can keep their existing component calls.
Pulumi state migration callbacks (the state migrations resource option) run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
Pulumi state migration callbacks must be idempotent and return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
Pulumi state migration callbacks rewrite state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A Pulumi component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
In a Pulumi component state migration result, each successor mapping connects an old URN omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a Pulumi component state migration callback returns no result.
The Pulumi state migrations option reference at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/#callback-api explains the callback API.

Component state migration state entries use the checkpoint resource format documented in the Pulumi developer docs deployment schema (pulumi-resource-state), including fields such as `urn`, `type`, `id`, `parent`, `provider`, `inputs`, and `outputs`.
The Pulumi developer docs deployment schema page at pulumi-developer-docs.readthedocs.io has a pulumi-resource-state section describing the checkpoint resource format.
A component state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using Pulumi update plans or targeted updates.
The Pulumi restrictions on state-changing migration results (with update plans or targeted updates) do not require removing an already-applied migration.
